entries.name: Bevy
entries.use_for: Build games in Rust with a data-driven ECS engine.
entries.why: Leading Rust engine with a fast-moving ecosystem and modular plugin design.

entries.name: Ebitengine
entries.use_for: Make 2D games in Go for desktop, mobile, web and consoles.
entries.why: The standard Go game engine; simple API, ships on Nintendo Switch.

entries.name: Excalibur
entries.use_for: Build 2D web games in TypeScript with a full engine (scenes, physics, input).
entries.why: TypeScript-first 2D engine (~2.4k stars, BSD-2) with good docs and tooling.

entries.name: Flame
entries.use_for: Build 2D games on Flutter for mobile, web and desktop.
entries.why: The main Flutter game engine with components, collisions and many bridge packages.

entries.name: Fyrox
entries.use_for: Make 2D and 3D games in Rust with a scene editor.
entries.why: Feature-rich Rust engine that ships with a full editor, unlike most Rust engines.

entries.name: GDevelop
entries.use_for: Make 2D/3D games with an event-based, no-code editor that exports to web and mobile.
entries.why: Open-source no-code engine (~28k stars); Core, GDJS and IDE are MIT.

license_verified.note: Core, GDJS, IDE and Extensions folders are MIT; name and logo are trademarks

entries.name: Godot
entries.use_for: Make 2D and 3D games with a full editor, GDScript or C#.
entries.why: Most popular open-source game engine (119k stars); MIT, no royalties, exports to all major platforms.

entries.name: KAPLAY
entries.use_for: Make 2D browser games quickly with a fun, beginner-friendly JS library.
entries.why: Community successor to Kaboom.js (~1.8k stars, MIT) with an active release cadence.

entries.name: libGDX
entries.use_for: Build cross-platform Java games for desktop, Android, iOS and web.
entries.why: Long-standing, mature JVM game framework with a large community.

entries.name: LÖVE
entries.use_for: Make 2D games in Lua with a small, fast framework.
entries.why: Beloved Lua 2D framework (~9k stars, zlib) behind many indie hits like Balatro.

license_verified.note: license.txt: LOVE is zlib; bundled deps have own licenses

entries.name: MonoGame
entries.use_for: Build cross-platform 2D/3D games in C# with an XNA-style framework.
entries.why: Proven framework behind Stardew Valley and Celeste; Ms-PL licensed.

entries.name: Open 3D Engine
entries.use_for: Build AAA-scale 3D games and simulations on an open engine.
entries.why: Linux Foundation engine from Amazon Lumberyard (~10k stars), Apache-2.0 or MIT.

license_verified.note: LICENSE.txt: Apache-2.0, or MIT at your option

entries.name: Panda3D
entries.use_for: Build 3D games and simulations in Python with a C++ core.
entries.why: Mature 3D engine (~5k stars, BSD-3) originally from Disney and Carnegie Mellon.

license_verified.note: LICENSE: modified BSD (3-clause), Carnegie Mellon University

entries.name: Phaser
entries.use_for: Make 2D browser games with Canvas and WebGL.
entries.why: The most popular HTML5 2D game framework (40k stars) with extensive examples.

entries.name: pygame-ce
entries.use_for: Make 2D games in Python on top of SDL.
entries.why: Actively maintained community fork of pygame (370+ contributors), drop-in compatible.

license_verified.note: README states LGPL-2.1-or-later; text in docs/LGPL.txt

entries.name: raylib
entries.use_for: Program games in C (or 70+ language bindings) with a simple, dependency-free API.
entries.why: Famously easy to learn; great for prototypes, jams and teaching. Zlib license.

entries.name: Ren'Py
entries.use_for: Build visual novels and story-driven games with a Python-based script language.
entries.why: The standard visual novel engine (~7k stars) behind thousands of commercial titles.

license_verified.note: Ren'Py itself MIT per sphinx/source/license.rst; some bundled parts LGPL

entries.name: Stride
entries.use_for: Make 3D games in C# with a full editor.
entries.why: MIT-licensed C# engine with editor; an open alternative for Unity developers.
